---

### **Recurrence Relation**

For all $ n \geq 0 $, define the sequence $ a(n) $ as:

- **Base cases**:
  $$
  a(0) = 0, \quad a(1) = 1
  $$

- **Recursive cases**:
  $$
  a(n) = 
  \begin{cases}
  a(n-4) + 1000 & \text{if } n \equiv 0 \pmod{4} \text{ and } n \geq 4 \\
  a(n-1) + 1 & \text{if } n \equiv 1 \pmod{4} \\
  a(n-1) + 375 & \text{if } n \equiv 2 \pmod{4} \\
  a(n-1) + 249 & \text{if } n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}
  \end{cases}
  $$

---

### **Explanation of the Recurrence**

- **When $ n \equiv 0 \pmod{4} $**:
  - This corresponds to the **first term of a new group**.
  - The value is 1000 more than the first term of the previous group, i.e., $ a(n-4) + 1000 $.

- **When $ n \equiv 1 \pmod{4} $**:
  - This is the **second term** in the group.
  - It is simply the previous term plus 1.

- **When $ n \equiv 2 \pmod{4} $**:
  - This is the **third term** in the group.
  - It is the previous term plus 375.

- **When $ n \equiv 3 \pmod{4} $**:
  - This is the **fourth term** in the group.
  - It is the previous term plus 249.

---

### **Example Calculation**

- $ a(0) = 0 $

- $ a(8) = a(4) + 1000 = 1000 + 1000 = 2000 $

This matches the expected pattern.
